citations.desc: Access and inspection of records and property; submission of itineraries.
citations.narrative:
A written itinerary was not submitted by the licensee to the Deputy Administrator prior to exhibition with overnight travel.
The licensee was in travel status at the time of inspection.
Failure to provide and update itinerary information may result in the inability to conduct an inspection to ensure the
welfare of the animals covered under the Animal Welfare Act.
The licensee must submit a written itinerary to the Deputy Administrator no sooner than 48 hours in advance of any travel
when exhibiting any animal overnight at any location other than the approved home site. The itinerary shall include all
information required in this section, but not limited to, the names, dates, and locations (with addresses) where the animals
will travel, be housed, and be exhibited, including all anticipated dates and locations (with addresses) for any stops and
layovers that allow or require removal of the animals from the transport enclosures.
Corrected at the time of the inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee (over the phone) and facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
